item.research_question: Can atomically thin high-entropy oxides be synthesized via naked metal ion self-assembly for proton exchange membrane electrolysis?
item.processing_route: Self-assembly technique using molten salts to desolvate metal ions from water molecules coordination
item.test_conditions: 0.5 M H2SO4 aqueous electrolyte, 80 °C, 1 A cm−2
key_findings: RuIrFeCoCrO2 requires an overpotential of 185 mV at 10 mA cm−2
Maintains high activity for over 1000 h in an acidic electrolyte
Cr, Co, and Ir sites contribute to the catalytic activity
Cr atoms weaken the Ru-O bond covalency and improve the catalyst stability
RuIrFeCoCrO2 electrode delivers a low overpotential of 185 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and stable operation over 1000 h
item.mechanism: The adsorption evolution mechanism (AEM) is proposed, where the weakened Ru-O bond covalency by Cr prohibits the leaching of Ru atoms and thus benefits the crystal stability
quotes: Designing efficient Ruthenium-based catalysts as practical anodes is of critical importance in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis
The contribution of each atom in the RuIrFeCoCrO2 to the electrocatalysis performance has been scrutinized

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can atomically thin high-entropy oxides be synthesized via naked metal ion self-assembly for proton exchange membrane electrolysis?. System: RuIrFeCoCrO2 high-entropy oxides. Processing: Self-assembly technique using molten salts to desolvate metal ions from water molecules coordination. Test conditions: 0.5 M H2SO4 aqueous electrolyte, 80 °C, 1 A cm−2. Findings: RuIrFeCoCrO2 requires an overpotential of 185 mV at 10 mA cm−2; Maintains high activity for over 1000 h in an acidic electrolyte; Cr, Co, and Ir sites contribute to the catalytic activity; Cr atoms weaken the Ru-O bond covalency and improve the catalyst stability; RuIrFeCoCrO2 electrode delivers a low overpotential of 185 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and stable operation over 1000 h. Mechanism: The adsorption evolution mechanism (AEM) is proposed, where the weakened Ru-O bond covalency by Cr prohibits the leaching of Ru atoms and thus benefits the crystal stability. Quote: "Designing efficient Ruthenium-based catalysts as practical anodes is of critical importance in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis"
